c.tagline: Cyprus's mosaic-rich harbour town where legend says Aphrodite rose from the sea.

taxi.fareNote: Urban taxis are metered; rural and intercity taxis use fixed zonal tariffs. Bolt coverage is limited, so most rides are booked by phone or picked up at ranks.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number; 199 also reaches police, ambulance, and fire in Cyprus.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Expect inflated drink prices and occasional bar scams along the Kato Paphos Bar Street nightlife strip.

hood_desc: The lower seafront town around the harbour, castle and the UNESCO-listed archaeological park with its Roman mosaics; the tourist heart, packed with hotels, tavernas and sights.
The upper old town (also called Ktima), built up the hillside around the covered market, Kennedy Square and the municipal gardens; more local, with shops, bakeries and everyday life.
The hotel strip running north from the harbour past the Tombs of the Kings, lined with resorts, beach bars and restaurants; convenient and lively, close to the sea.
A resort area about 12 km north near Peyia, built around a sheltered sandy bay and the gateway to the wild Akamas peninsula; relaxed and family-friendly.
A traditional village just east of Kato Paphos, known for its five-domed Agia Paraskevi church and Cyprus delight sweets; quieter and residential with easy beach access.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: OSYPA buses run roughly 6:00 AM to about 8:00-11:00 PM depending on the route, with reduced service in winter.
transit.note: Paphos has no rail or metro; the OSYPA bus network links Kato Paphos, the upper town (Ktima), Coral Bay and the airport. Service thins in the evenings and in winter, so taxis fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the driver (around €1.50 single, €5 day ticket, more at night). There is no contactless smartcard system as of 2026.

bus: OSYPA Paphos city and district buses
Intercity buses to Limassol and Nicosia

transit.m: Airport bus (route 612/613) to Kato Paphos and Karavella station (~30-40 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants if a service charge is not already included; rounding up for taxis and cafes is appreciated.
